algorithm: Validate nonempty rectangular palette-10 grid no larger than 30x30 and exact finite tensor shapes in [-9,9].
Count each present color. Sort colors by descending rank.weight[0]*count, breaking ties by ascending color ID.
Expand each color by its ORIGINAL input count. No learned color lookup, no output-size prediction.
argmax(scan.axis) chooses row-major or column-major coordinates. argmax(scan.row) and argmax(scan.col) choose ascending/descending coordinate order.
Fill those coordinates with the ordered colors and return the original shape.
integration: One additive function and versioned TEMPLATES entry in skillcore.py; never change existing template behavior.
Existing make_cell/cell_reference/typed-bank contracts support the declared interface and layout.
Separate tensor-only native packet and raw provenance would be required before any author call; current direct-grid baseline stays separate.
No specialist-service admission change is necessary for an offline research probe. No generators, runtime, API, deployment or arbitrary source required.
interface: existing cellforge-cell-interface/1; integer rank-two palette-10 grid to same-shape grid
invariants: At most 900 input/output cells and 10 color groups. Bounded deterministic host function; no authored code evaluation.
Output shape and per-color multiplicities always equal input, including zero and random controls.
All-zero parameters have defined tie behavior. Equal color counts use fixed documented color-ID tie break; no evidence that this tie policy transfers.

random_baseline_warning.derivation: One rank sign times three independent binary traversal choices; continuous symmetric random tensors, no ties.
random_baseline_warning.scope: Analytical behavior-space estimate for these demonstrations, not a measured ARC result.

recommendation: Keep the host-inferred program as a baseline now. Do not spend an extra author merely to celebrate solving this small selector space; if implemented later, report matched-random luck and limited semantics openly.
scientific_limit: Host supplies counting, sorting and placement algorithms. Tensor coefficients choose coarse behavior. This does not learn the algorithm or constitute a neural architecture discovery.
